classification.difficultyReason: Choose auxiliary right triangles and midpoint constructions to realise exact surd and reciprocal-surd lengths.

content.prompt: How would you construct intervals of the following lengths? Discuss with your teacher.

answer.short: Construct a unit-square diagonal, then use it and a unit segment as perpendicular sides. The new hypotenuse has length $\sqrt3$.
answer.worked:
Draw a unit square; its diagonal has length $\sqrt2$. Construct a perpendicular unit segment at one end of that diagonal and join the free endpoints.
$$\begin{align*}h^2&=(\sqrt2)^2+1^2\\h^2&=3\\h&=\sqrt3.\end{align*}$$

answer.short: Bisect the diagonal of a unit square: $\frac{\sqrt2}{2}=\frac1{\sqrt2}$.
answer.worked:
Construct a unit square and draw its diagonal. Bisect the diagonal.
$$\begin{align*}d^2&=1^2+1^2\\d&=\sqrt2\\\frac d2&=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}=\frac1{\sqrt2}.\end{align*}$$

answer.short: Construct a square of side 2; its diagonal has length $\sqrt8$.
answer.worked:
Construct perpendicular segments of length 2 from a common endpoint and join their free endpoints.
$$\begin{align*}d^2&=2^2+2^2\\d^2&=8\\d&=\sqrt8.\end{align*}$$

Construct a unit square and draw its diagonal of length $\sqrt2$. Bisect the diagonal, then bisect one half. Each quarter has length
$$\begin{align*}\ell&=\frac{\sqrt2}{4}\\\ell&=\frac1{2\sqrt2}\\\ell&=\frac1{\sqrt8}.\end{align*}$$
